apply_template(obj: UndergroundLineType, Sbase: float, logger: Logger | None = None) → None[source]

Apply one Cable System to this line atomically.

The resistance copied to DcLine is the static per-unit value used by network compilation. Inductance and capacitance remain canonical in UndergroundLineType and are converted on demand by the dynamic consumers. The branch rating is intentionally preserved until the public DC pole voltage convention is defined.

Parameters:

  • obj – Cable System to apply.

  • Sbase – System power base in MVA.

  • logger – Optional logger receiving validation failures.

Returns:

None.

get_applied_dynamic_values_pu_seconds(Sbase: float) → Tuple[float, float] | None[source]

Convert the associated physical cable data for dynamic consumers.

This method returns None when the line has no physical cable evidence. It does not apply a simulation fallback or write a log.

Parameters:

Sbase – System power base in MVA.

Total series inductance and shunt capacitance in p.u. seconds, or None when no physical cable type is associated.

get_dynamic_values_pu_seconds(Sbase: float, logger: Logger | None) → Tuple[float, float][source]

Get the physical cable coefficients required by a dynamic simulation.

A line without a physical cable template remains usable as a purely resistive branch. The missing optional dynamics are reported instead of stopping the simulation.

Parameters:

  • Sbase – System power base in MVA.

  • logger – Optional driver logger receiving the resistive-fallback warning.

Total series inductance and shunt capacitance in p.u. seconds.

change_base(Sbase_old: float, Sbase_new: float) → None[source]

Refer the same physical line to another system power base.

Voltage bases stay fixed. Sequence impedances scale with power base, while shunts and stored phase admittances scale with its reciprocal. Invalid bases leave the line unchanged; ratios and transformed values must remain within the representable floating-point range.

Parameters:

  • Sbase_old – Existing three-phase system power base in MVA.

  • Sbase_new – Requested three-phase system power base in MVA.

Returns:

None.

VeraGridEngine.Devices.Branches.overhead_line_type.calc_L_int(is_tube, r, q)[source]

Calculates internal inductance of solid or tubular conductor Note that calculations assume uniform current distribution in the conductor, thus conductor stranding is not taken into account.

Usage:

L_int = calc_L_int(type, r, q)

where:
type is ‘solid’ or ‘tube’

r is the radius of the conductor [m] q is the radius of the inner tube [m]

Returns:

L_int the internal inductance of the conductor [H/m]

Calculates self impedance term [Ohm/km] NOTE: No allowance has been made for skin effects :param R_int: AC conductor resistance [Ohm/km] :param is_tube: is it a tube conductor? otherwise is solid :param r_outer: radius of the conductor [m] :param r_inner: radius of the inner tube [m] :param y_i: height of conductor i above ground [m] :param f: frequency [Hz] :param rho: earth resistivity [Ohm.m] :param err_tol: error tolerance for the calculation (default = 1e-6) :param use_dubanton_aprox: Use dubanton’s approximation (default = False) :param gmr: Specified GMR in metres; zero uses the solid/tubular geometry. :return: self impedance term of line impedance matrix [Ohm/km]

Calculates mutual impedance term [Ohm/km] :param y_i: height of conductor i above ground [m] :param y_j: height of conductor j above ground [m] :param x_i: x position of the conductor i [m] :param x_j: x position of the conductor j [m] :param f: frequency [Hz] :param rho: earth resistivity [ohm·m] :param err_tol: error tolerance for the calculation (default = 1e-6) :param use_dubanton_aprox: Use dubanton’s approximation (default = False) :return:self impedance term of line impedance matrix (Ohm/km)

VeraGridEngine.Devices.Branches.overhead_line_type.calc_z_matrix(wires_in_tower: ListOfWires, f: float = 50, rho: float = 100, use_dubanton_aprox: bool = False)[source]

Impedance matrix :param wires_in_tower: WireInTower :param f: system frequency (Hz) :param rho: earth resistivity :param use_dubanton_aprox: Use dubanton’s approximation (default = False) :return: 4 by 4 impedance matrix where the order of the phases is: N, A, B, C

VeraGridEngine.Devices.Branches.overhead_line_type.carsons(is_self: bool, h_i: float, h_k: float, x_ik: float, f: float, rho: float, err_tol: float = 1e-06)[source]

Calculate Carson earth-return corrections (Rp, Xp), in Ohm/km.

Heights and horizontal separation are in metres, f in Hz and rho in Ohm.m. err_tol bounds the magnitude of terms in the dimensionless Carson series. The EMTP series is summed in complete groups of four terms, so a vanishing angular factor cannot prematurely terminate the calculation. Coefficient recurrence: Carson implementation in https://doi.org/10.5772/58383.

set_impedance_correction_values(correction_real: ndarray, correction_imag: ndarray) → bool[source]

Install exact real and imaginary impedance factors by tap position.

The stored branch impedance is the neutral reference. Each factor is applied only when numerical data is compiled, which keeps the tap characteristic reusable after editing or serialisation.

Parameters:

  • correction_real – Non-negative resistance factors.

  • correction_imag – Non-negative reactance factors.

Returns:

True when both complete arrays were accepted.

set_tap_module(tap_module: float) → float[source]

Set the tap position closest to the tap module :param tap_module: float value of the tap module

set_tap_module_phase_values(tap_modules: ndarray, tap_phases: ndarray) → bool[source]

Install one exact discrete complex-tap table.

This table is required by importers whose native tap law contains a fixed vector-group shift, a winding-side reciprocal or another relationship that cannot be represented by the generic dV and asymmetry parameters alone. Core tap-configuration setters still call recalc(), intentionally returning the object to its generic law.

Parameters:

  • tap_modules – Positive tap magnitudes by zero-based position.

  • tap_phases – Unwrapped tap phases in radians by position.

Returns:

True when the complete table was accepted.

class VeraGridEngine.Devices.Branches.transformerNw.TransformerNW(idtag: str | None = None, code: str = '', name: str = 'TransformerNW', bus0: Bus | None = None, winding_count: int | None = None, buses: Sequence[Bus | None] | None = None, active: bool = True, Pfe: float = 0.0, I0: float = 0.0, x: float = 0.0, y: float = 0.0, build_status: BuildStatus = Commissioned)[source]

Bases: PhysicalDevice

Generic N-winding transformer represented as a set of windings connected to a common internal star bus.

The leakage data is stored per winding. Shared core-loss data is represented by Pfe and I0 at the transformer level and mapped through get_impedances. To avoid counting the magnetizing branch multiple times, the resulting shunt admittance is assigned to the first winding only.

get_branch_dynamic_templates(device_type: DeviceType, logger: Logger) → tuple[source]

Share electrical data without assigning AC dynamic models to DC or vice versa.

get_dc_parameters(conductor: int = 1) → tuple[float, float, float][source]

Return Rdc [ohm/km], L [H/km] and C [F/km] for one DC conductor.

For a physical system, conductor is its global phase number. The existing sheath-reduced matrices supply the diagonal L/C at freq; Rdc comes from the physical core, without AC skin/earth-return losses. A scalar DcLine does not represent mutual coupling between conductors. Parameter-only systems use R, X and C (or B), including imported DGS equivalents whose construction is unknown.

get_dc_values(Sbase: float, length: float, line_Vnom: float, conductor: int = 1) → tuple[float, float, float][source]

Return total DC R in p.u. and L/C in p.u. seconds.

Keep the historical DC conversion: Zbase = Vnom**2/Sbase, Rpu = R*length/Zbase, Lpu = L*length/Zbase, Cpu = C*length*Zbase.

get_values(Sbase: float, length: float, circuit_index: int = 1, round_vals: bool = True, Vnom: float | None = None) → tuple[float, float, float, float, float, float, float][source]
